result:
The fitted BRDF rule was right. The arm failed because another change (#283, landed 2026-09-25) had started feeding the BRDF stage the wrong input between the fit and the arm. I've posted the per-pixel diff, the broken assumption and a patch on #315. PR #375 is marked ready; the patch itself is not rendered yet, because I'm not allowed to commit `psh.c`.

**Per-pixel diff of the failed arm:** the pixels that changed are exactly the golden's 614 wedge pixels, and nothing outside the wedge moved. So drawing (coverage) is fine and the colour lookup is wrong. That is the brief's "same pixels, different colours" case. Not one pixel matches its golden:
- Green is 89 (volume texel 22) on every pixel, where the golden has 246 (texel 61).
- At (639,479) ours reads (178,89,222) and the golden (198,246,222).
- Every pixel is an exact volume-texture colour, so the 3D sampler, nearest filtering and `dots_needed 0` all worked as the fit assumed.

**The assumption that broke:** the fit assumed stages 0 and 1 hand the BRDF stage their whole 16-bit angle fields. #283 splits these textures into bytes for every later stage except those listed in `stage_consumed_raw()`, and BRDF isn't on that list. So the BRDF stage read theta's low byte and phi's high byte instead. #283 is in the arm's base but not in the commit the fit was made against.

Scored over the 610 wedge pixels the model covers (whole-texel matches):

| what stages 0/1 deliver | matches the arm's render | matches the golden |
|---|---|---|
| whole 16-bit fields (the fit) | 0 | 605 |
| bytes, as #283 delivers them | 598 | 0 |

The deciding number: the light's theta is 0xf658. Read as a whole field that gives texel 61, the golden's value. Its low byte gives texel 22, which is what we rendered on every pixel. The 12 pixels where the bytes model misses are all ties at a cube-map texel edge. Using whole fields, each of them lands on the golden's value, so the model predicts no misses on those 610 pixels.

**Next step:** `docs/lanes/brdf315b/brdf315b-psh.diff`. It is the original BRDF change plus a BRDF case in `stage_consumed_raw()`, so the two stages BRDF reads keep their whole fields.
- It applies at the tip and on top of both lanes holding `psh.c` (#373, #367).
- It passes a syntax-only compile.
- One side effect no capture covers: a sign-flagged texture feeding BRDF would now reach it unsigned. This test sets no sign flags.

**Not done:**
- No prediction is registered and there was no device run. Both need a commit to `psh.c`, which is held by lane.fog278 and lent to lane.y16bump10.
- I filed a board request (`$DISPATCH_DIR/board-requests/brdf315b.md`) for `psh.c` after those PRs merge. The prediction is written up in NOTES section 4, ready for whoever commits the patch: all three BRDF captures from 614 differing pixels to at most 4 each, and (639,479) reading (198,246,222,255).

Preflight passes, and `Files:` matches the diff.

The Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive connectors need authorizing in claude.ai's connector settings before this session can use them; I didn't need them here.
